findings.title: Dead-code comparison on dayjs objects with ===
findings.body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two newly created dayjs object references with `===`, which will always be false since dayjs() returns new objects. The intended check for a zero-length override (start === end) never triggers, so this branch is unreachable dead code.

findings.title: Working-hours bound check uses start time for both start and end
findings.body: In the fallback check for whether a slot is within normal working hours: `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime`, ignoring the slot's actual end time (which should use `slotEndTime`). This makes the `end > workingHour.endTime` check meaningless (since start==end), so slots that end after working hours (e.g. due to eventLength) will incorrectly be considered within bounds, causing availability to be computed incorrectly for slots overlapping the end of working hours.

findings.title: organizerTimeZone omitted from dateOverrides path for currentSeats busy check
findings.body: The last `checkIfIsAvailable` call (used when checking selectedSlots/currentSeats-based busy times) does pass `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone` but does not pass `dateOverrides` or `workingHours`, unlike other call sites. Since `checkIfIsAvailable` defaults these to `[]`, this invocation will skip the date-override/working-hours logic entirely for this code path, meaning date overrides for a specific user are not respected here, potentially allowing booking of a slot that is actually blocked (or vice versa) when selected/seat slots are involved.

findings.title: override.timeZone may be undefined causing wrong offset
findings.body: `override.timeZone` is typed optional (`TimeRange.timeZone?: string`), but `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` is called without a fallback. If `timeZone` is undefined for an override (e.g. constructed elsewhere without setting it), `dayjs().tz(undefined)` behavior is implementation-dependent and could silently produce an incorrect offset, defeating the timezone-adjustment fix this PR intends to add.

findings.title: New timezone test does not actually exercise different invitee timezone behavior meaningfully
findings.body: The new test asserts that querying with timezone +6:00 yields the exact same UTC slot list as +5:30, which trivially passes since results are always converted to UTC Z notation and compared by UTC string regardless of input tz; it doesn't verify that slots shift according to the override's organizer timezone when the invitee timezone differs from organizer's, so the actual bug (date overrides not adjusting per attendee timezone) is only weakly covered.
